cylinders.typicalUse: Recreational single tank (warm water, training, sidemount)
cylinders.notes: Standard rental tank globally; becomes positively buoyant near end of dive. Weight and buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL80 sheet (full -0.80 kg, +1.54 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve); empty and at-50-bar are derived from the 500 psi row.

cylinders.typicalUse: Recreational single tank (Asia, some EU regions)
cylinders.notes: Common in Asian dive markets; larger and heavier than AL80. Weight and water volume from the Luxfer P3080V (12.0 L, 16.5 kg, 204 mm; Luxfer scuba spec sheet 2022, which prints no buoyancy). Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

cylinders.typicalUse: Recreational single tank (smaller divers, shorter dives)
cylinders.notes: Good option between AL63 and AL80; popular for travel and sidemount.
Popular with small-frame divers or kids; lighter but same diameter as AL80. Weight and buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL63 sheet (full -1.1 kg, +0.77 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).
Compact stage/deco bottle; manageable for warm-water tech dives. Weight and buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL50 sheet (full -1.13 kg, +0.36 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).
Common oxygen bottle for deco; good trim when clipped to left side. Weight and buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL40 sheet (full -0.32 kg, +1.13 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).
Pony bottle for emergency gas; small enough for travel or boat use. Weight and buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL30 sheet (full -0.68 kg, 0 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).

Very small bailout bottle; close to neutral when empty. Water volume is Luxfer's true LAL19 figure (2.87 L), so its real-gas free gas reads a touch over the marketed 19. Buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL19 sheet (full -0.60 kg, -0.05 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).
Usually mounted for drysuit argon inflation; rarely used for breathing gas. Buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL13 sheet (full -0.80 kg, -0.40 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).

Most common steel cylinder in Europe; stays negative. Weight from Faber's cylinder database (EN 1964-1 build, without valve, 171 mm): 14.1 kg; the 2023 design (EN ISO 9809-1:2019) weighs 13.3 kg, about 0.7 kg more buoyant. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

Very dense; allows more gas but heavier topside and affects trim. Weight from Faber's cylinder database (EN 1964-1 build, without valve, 171 mm): 18.0 kg. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

Heavy but long bottom time; stays negative when empty. Weight from Faber's cylinder database (EN 1964-1 build, without valve, 203 mm): 18.2 kg; the 2023 design weighs 16.7 kg (Faber press release, 14 April 2023), about 1.3 kg more buoyant. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

Often used as twin 10s for balanced doubles in cold water. Weight from Faber's cylinder database (EN 1964-1 build, without valve, 171 mm): 12.2 kg; the 2023 design weighs 11.5 kg. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

Popular compact steel; often used as twin 10.5s in Europe. Weight from Faber's cylinder database (EN 1964-1 build, without valve, 178 mm): 12.9 kg; the 2023 design weighs 12.0 kg. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

Stage/deco bottle for cold water; remains negative throughout. Weight from Faber's cylinder database (EN 1964-1 build, without valve, 140 mm): 8.5 kg; the 2023 design weighs 8.2 kg. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

Standard 3L rebreather bottle; fits most CCR frames. Weight from Faber's cylinder database (EN 1964-1 build, without valve, 100 mm): 4.8 kg; the 2023 design weighs 4.6 kg. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

Popular cave/wreck tank; becomes positive if not overfilled. Water volume, weight and buoyancy are the Faber LP85 (31.2 lb; full -3.80 lb, +2.32 lb at 500 psi, in sea water with valve); empty and at-50-bar are derived from the 500 psi row.
Cave/wreck doubles workhorse; roughly neutral when empty.

Good trim and buoyancy; favorite single for drysuit divers. The 12.9 L water volume, weight and buoyancy are the Faber FX100 (34.0 lb; full -8.41 lb, -0.59 lb at 500 psi, in sea water with valve); empty and at-50-bar are derived from the 500 psi row. The Worthington/PST X7-100 is a different cylinder (~11.6 L).

Tall and heavy; lots of gas for single-tank tech or long rec dives. Weight and water volume from the Worthington X7-120 (15.3 L, 18.0 kg without valve; XS Scuba's Worthington sheet). The sheet lists -5.0 kg full and -0.9 kg empty with valve; physics sits 0.2 to 0.3 kg above. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.
Popular tech diving cylinder; good balance of capacity and trim. Weight and buoyancy from the Faber FX117 sheet (37.6 lb; full -9.12 lb, +0.35 lb at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).

Gas monster; heavy and long, often awkward for smaller divers. Weight and water volume from the Worthington X8-130 (16.0 L, 20.3 kg without valve; XS Scuba's Worthington sheet). Low confidence: the sheet's -0.9 kg empty and its 131.4 cu ft rating both point to about 16.7 L, so its volume or weight is off. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

Faber's largest single (sometimes called a 130). Heavy, but floats when empty. Weight and buoyancy from the Faber FX133 sheet (42.4 lb; full -9.08 lb, +1.45 lb at 500 psi, in sea water with valve); empty and at-50-bar are derived from the 500 psi row.

Compact CCR O₂ bottle; easy to travel with and replace. Weight from Faber's cylinder database (EN 1964-1 build, without valve, 100 mm): 2.6 kg. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

Standard diluent cylinder for most CCR units; often filled to 232 bar. Weight from Faber's cylinder database (EN 1964-1 build, without valve, 100 mm): 3.6 kg. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

cylinders.typicalUse: Longer rec single / big gas in warm water
cylinders.notes: High-capacity aluminum; tall and heavy. Weight and buoyancy from the Luxfer LAL100 sheet (full -2.10 kg, +0.86 kg at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).

Compact steel; stays negative when empty. Water volume, weight and buoyancy are the Faber FX80 (28.3 lb; full -8.05 lb, -1.74 lb at 500 psi, in sea water with valve); empty and at-50-bar are derived from the 500 psi row.

High-capacity HP steel; stays negative. Weight and water volume from the Worthington X8-119 (14.8 L, 19.3 kg without valve; XS Scuba's Worthington sheet). Low confidence: the sheet's -0.9 kg empty and its 123 cu ft rating both point to about 15.6 L, so its volume or weight is off. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

Popular small LP cylinder in the US; often overfilled in practice. Weight and water volume from the Faber LP50 (7.8 L, 8.6 kg; Faber LP spec sheet). Neither the Worthington nor the PST sheet lists an LP50. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

cylinders.typicalUse: Vintage/ubiquitous US steel; still common on boats
cylinders.notes: Classic 2250 psi steel 72; slim profile; about neutral when empty. No sheet prints its water volume: 12.2 L is derived from the rated 71.55 cu ft at 2475 psi (real-gas air at 70 °F); the dataset's former 13.2 L was the error. The weight (13.7 kg) is the one that gives the published empty buoyancy (0 lb with valve; US Divers figures quoted on ScubaBoard); the 26 lb (11.8 kg) quoted beside it would make the cylinder +1.6 kg empty at that volume. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.
Large LP steel; heavy topside; remains negative when empty.
High-capacity LP steel; excellent for long tech dives and doubles. Weight and buoyancy from the Faber LP108 sheet (41 lb; full -5.0 lb, +3.0 lb at 500 psi, in sea water with valve).
Common EU large single; heavy but lots of gas.

Compact EU steel; often used as twin 8.5s. Faber makes no 8.5 L. Weight from a retailer listing of the ECS 8.5 L 232 bar 140 mm (11.0 kg, without valve); low confidence, other brands list 10.0 to 11.9 kg. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.
A CCR bottle size seen on some frames. Weight unsourced; buoyancy computed from it. Faber's database lists no 2.7 L (its 100 mm sizes are 2, 2.5 and 3 L), and no other maker's sheet was found.

The EU-standard 232 bar rating of the compact CCR bottle. Weight from Faber's cylinder database (EN 1964-1 build, without valve, 100 mm): 2.8 kg; the UK BS 5045-7 build weighs 2.6 kg. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

The EU-standard 232 bar rating of the common CCR diluent cylinder. Weight from Faber's cylinder database (EN 1964-1 build, without valve, 100 mm): 3.8 kg; the UK BS 5045-7 build weighs 3.4 kg. Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.

The light 200 bar Faber 12L; popular for sidemount in Europe, and slightly positive when empty. Weight from Faber's cylinder database (EN 1964-1 build, without valve, 171 mm): 12.0 kg. The 203 mm build weighs 13.6 kg (12.3 kg in the 2023 design). Buoyancy is computed from the weight and water volume (scripts/cylinder-buoyancy-other.py), in sea water with a standard valve.
